News.title: Doctors thought girl with 148 broken bones was being abused, but they were wrong
News.content:
Doctors thought girl with 148 broken bones was being abused, but they were wrong

When parents Kendra and Eric took their daughter to hospital they were placed under investigation

View 5 Images Hadley in hospital

A mum says doctors suspected she was abusing her own baby because she had a number of unexplained fractures, but thenm it was found she had a rare health condition. Kendra Larsen and her husband Eric, came under suspicion when their newborn daughter, Hadley, was injured.

‌



But Hadley has a rare “China doll” condition that makes her bones so fragile they can snap in an instant. In total, she has suffered 148 fractures. Hadley was born with Osteogenesis Imperfecta (OI), also known as brittle bone disease, a condition that stops the body from producing enough collagen to keep bones strong.

‌



But at the time, her parents had no idea. “When we first took Hadley to hospital, we truly had no idea what was wrong,” said Kendra, 44, from Idaho Falls, Idaho, US. “She was only four weeks old. We thought maybe she had hip dysplasia or something related to her hip, so they started by doing X-rays of that area. That’s when everything changed.

‌



View 5 Images Hadley after breaking her leg

“The X-rays showed that Hadley actually had two fractures that were at different stages of healing. Because of that, the doctors ordered a full skeletal survey, which means they X-ray everything in the body. When those results came back, they found two more fractures.

‌



“Suddenly our tiny four-week-old baby had four fractures, and we had absolutely no explanation for how it could have happened.”

The nightmare escalated when doctors began to suspect something far more sinister. Kendra recalled how one medic told them he needed to rule out whether they had caused brain damage to their child, now 13. She said: “Hearing those words as a parent is something I will never forget. We had gone to the hospital scared and desperate for help for our bab, and in an instant the focus shifted away from Hadley and onto us - as if we might have been the ones who hurt her.

“Suddenly we weren’t just parents trying to help our injured newborn; we were being looked at as possible child abusers. It is one of the worst feelings you can imagine as a parent. Shortly after that, a doctor came in and told us Hadley was being admitted to the hospital for her safety.

‌



View 5 Images Hadley with another broken bone

“Those words are incredibly hard for any parent to hear, especially when you are already terrified and confused. What made it even harder was that our newborn baby had multiple fractures and was clearly in pain, and we were trying to process everything while also feeling like we were being treated with suspicion instead of support.

‌



“Thankfully, Hadley had a pediatrician who was familiar with OI. He called the hospital and told them he did not believe this was child abuse and that he believed Hadley likely had the condition.”

Kendra said: “We still had to meet with investigators to go through the process of proving we had not hurt our own child. All of this was happening while we were caring for a fragile four-week-old baby who we were desperately trying to protect.

View 5 Images Kendra, Hadley and Eric

‌



“It took about four months for the blood work and testing to confirm the diagnosis. Those months felt incredibly long and heavy. Every day, we were caring for our baby while also carrying the weight of being suspected of something we would never do.

“When we finally received the official diagnosis, it brought a sense of relief, but it also brought a lot of sadness. By that point we had done enough research to understand just how serious OI can be. In some ways, getting the answer we had been searching for also meant letting go of the hope that it might be something less severe or something she might simply grow out of.

‌



“The diagnosis gave us clarity, but it also marked the beginning of a completely different journey than we had ever imagined for our daughter.”

View 5 Images Kendra, Hadley and Eric

Article continues below

Kendra says the ordeal changed their lives forever. She added: “Looking back, it was one of the hardest chapters of our lives. But it also showed us how important awareness is. When rare conditions like OI aren’t immediately recognised, families can find themselves in incredibly painful and isolating situations.

“Today, when I look at Hadley, her strength, her determination, the way she shows up with light and joy even after everything she has been through, I’m reminded that her story is so much bigger than those early moments of fear. She has turned what started as one of the most terrifying experiences of our lives into a life that inspires and connects with so many people.

“And that little four-week-old baby they once questioned is now one of the strongest people I know.”

News.title: M8 traffic LIVE: Glasgow motorway closed at rush hour sparking travel mayhem
News.content:
A busy motorway has been plunged into chaos this morning with a large stretch of the road closed as commuters head to work.

Drivers are facing long queues on the M8 eastbound in Glasgow - Scotland's busiest motorway - between junctions 18 and 15. It comes after the road closed overnight following roadworks which have overrun, causing it to remain closed this morning.

There is currently no access to the route from junction 16 Craighall, junction 18 Charing Cross, and junction 19 Anderston.

News.title: Liverpool care home left residents 'starving' and only bathed them once a month
News.content:
Liverpool care home left residents 'starving' and only bathed them once a month

Christopher Grange Residential Care in West Derby received the lowest possible CQC rating after inspectors found residents without adequate food, hygiene or care

View Image Christopher Grange care home was given the lowest possible CQC rating (Image: Google)

Residents at a care home were left "starving" in bed and were only bathed once a month, a damning report has found.

‌



Inspectors condemned Christopher Grange Residential Care in West Derby, Liverpool, where residents were left with "extremely long toenails" and were only bathed once a month. The facility has been placed into special measures by the Care Quality Commission following four days of inspections in October and November 2025. Fifty-seven people resided at the home at the time, some of whom had dementia.

‌



Operator Christopher Grange Ltd was found to be breaching regulations around safe care, staffing, nutrition, hydration and safeguarding. The home was given the lowest possible rating.

‌



'Starving'

The inspector discovered that several people receiving bed care had not been provided with sufficient food and drink, with extended periods between meals or fluids being offered. One individual did not receive personal care until late morning, and their records revealed they had not received continence support for more than 12 hours despite their care plan stating they required full assistance, reports the Liverpool Echo.

Records revealed they had been awake for several hours without being offered a drink, and the person told inspectors they were "starving". Inspectors discovered the resident did not receive breakfast until later in the day.

Another individual did not receive any fluids or personal care until late morning. They had not been offered fluids for 15 hours. Residents with diabetes were discovered to have been denied proper food and drink, including breakfasts missed on several days running and delayed meals on other occasions. Inspectors found people were shedding weight without suitable monitoring or action being taken.

‌



Residents 'soaked through'

Personal care records revealed residents were abandoned for extended periods without assistance for their toileting requirements. One resident informed inspectors they were left "soaked through" at times in the lounge, stating: "It's so uncomfortable". One individual had gone without continence support for over 12 hours despite their care plan stipulating they needed complete assistance.

Documentation examined by CQC inspectors revealed some residents received a shower just once monthly. A resident told the inspector: "I would like a shower more often but only get one every few weeks now as I need support from staff." When questioned about the circumstances, staff informed inspectors: "We just do not have the time to care for people properly no more".

Inspectors discovered numerous residents had "extremely long toenails", and one person was experiencing pain and discomfort due to overgrown toenails having not received chiropody care for over two years.

‌



44-minute wait for help

The report revealed staffing shortages meant residents were left waiting for extended periods without assistance. At one point during the inspections, 18 residents had called for help, with one call remaining unanswered for 44 minutes and 48 seconds. The registered manager informed inspectors: "So many staff are leaving due to the added pressures caused by staffing levels on each unit being cut." Other employees expressed feeling under "huge amounts of pressure", with numerous individuals revealing they were exploring other job opportunities.

One family member commented: "The staff are so busy and morale is low, they never get a minute." A resident shared: "I am resigned to having male carers to carry out personal duties because they are short of staff you have to depend on whoever is there, but I feel as though there is a loss of dignity, I would prefer a female member of staff."

'Visibly dirty'

Inspectors discovered that stand aids, wheelchairs and walking aids were "visibly dirty", noting that shower heads and shower chairs required cleaning, and communal toilets were unclean. Carpets were "heavily stained" and the environment was described as "tired" and "hard to keep clean".

‌



Inspectors determined that the provider failed to ensure medicines and treatments were safe, adding: "We found issues with cleanliness and infection control across all units."

'We understand the concern this may cause'

A spokesperson for Christopher Grange Ltd responded: "We acknowledge the findings of the recent CQC report and understand the concern this may cause to residents, families, and the wider community. Christopher Grange has been under new ownership and management since July 2025, following a period of significant challenge prior to our involvement. Since taking over, we have treated these findings with the utmost seriousness and have taken decisive action to address long standing issues.

"A new management team is now in place, supported by a strengthened governance framework to ensure that all aspects of care are effectively monitored, audited, and maintained to the highest standards. We are actively implementing a comprehensive and robust improvement plan, developed in close collaboration with the CQC and Liverpool City Council. This plan addresses all areas identified in the report and is being closely monitored to ensure sustained and measurable progress.

Article continues below

"Encouragingly, meaningful improvements are already underway, and early changes are having a positive impact on the quality and safety of care being delivered. We are working closely with healthcare professionals, regulators, and families to ensure transparency and accountability throughout this process. Christopher Grange has a long-standing presence within the local community, and we remain fully committed to restoring confidence and delivering the high standards of care that every resident deserves. Our priority remains, as always, the safety, dignity, and wellbeing of everyone who calls Christopher Grange home."

News.title: Costa hotel explosion horror as dozens evacuated and smoke visible for miles
News.content:
Dozens of tourists were forced to flee a hotel at a popular holiday resort after an explosion tore through the building, sparking a fire visible for miles.

Part of the fifth floor of the four-star Olas Hotel in the Costa Tropical resort of Almunecar, around 50 miles east of Malaga, was badly damaged in the blast, which left one man injured.

The hotel was 60% full with guests arriving for the start of Easter break when the blast occurred. The chaos unfolded as workers from energy firm Repsol were refilling fuel tanks for the establishment’s boiler on the building's terrace.

Flames quickly engulfed the top level with a massive plume of smoke rising from the hotel visible from several miles away. Emergency responders raced to the scene before evacuating holidaymakers as fire crews tackled the blaze.

Image: @informativost5 /X) @informativost5 /X)

An injured man, who was the driver of the propane gas lorry, was taken to Santa Ana Hospital in the nearby town of Motril. Two firefighters were also treated for smoke inhalation.

An investigation into the incident is underway following frantic efforts to find tourists staying at the hotel alternative accommodation in the area.

A spokesman for a regional government-run emergency response coordination centre said: "One person has been injured following an explosion that occurred yesterday on the roof of a hotel in Almunecar, in the province of Granada.

"At 1.10pm, the emergency line received the first of nearly fifteen calls reporting an explosion on the roof of a five-storey hotel on a street called Avenida de Europa.

"A mobile intensive care unit and a medical team were mobilised, as well as the Civil Guard, the Provincial Fire Brigade Consortium and the Local Police. Two volunteers from the Almunecar Local Civil Protection Group also travelled to the scene in a vehicle.

Image: @informativost5 /X) @informativost5 /X)

"The injured person was the individual who was refilling the boiler with gas in the laundry room on the fifth floor. He suffered head injuries. The incident caused material damage to the top floor of the building and led to the precautionary evacuation of guests."

It was not immediately clear this morning when the building will be declared safe for guests at the hotel, which is better known in the area by its old name of Hotel Carmen, to return.

Local mayor Juan Jose Ruiz Joya said it was a "miracle" none of the 44 guests affected were killed or injured. He said: "The area most affected was unoccupied at the time, which prevented a greater tragedy. We should be relieved nothing serious happened despite the explosion, which was quite powerful.

"The explosion caused part of the roof to collapse onto the street, but this did not result in any accidents either. The damage was mainly to property."

Hotel Olas describes itself online as a "Mediterranean retreat by the sea." It adds: "Located in the heart of Almunecar, next to Majuelo Park, in the shadow of San Miguel Castle and just a four-minute walk from the beach. Our simple, welcoming Andalusian-style hotel is ideal for those looking to combine relaxation, fine dining and culture.”

Officials have not specified if any British or Irish tourists were staying at the hotel when the explosion occurred.

News.title: 'I died for 10 minutes and time-travelled into the future - death is a door'
News.content:
'I died for 10 minutes and time-travelled into the future - death is a door'

Rubi says life in the future is more peaceful, and coming back to this world was 'the real hell'

View 4 Images Rubi fell seriously ill and ended up in a coma

A woman says she time-travelled into a parallel universe and spent five years in the future after a life-threatening blood clot left her brain dead. Rubi Rolgue felt like life was finally falling into place.

‌



The 24-year-old had just gotten married, moved cities and was months away from finishing her degree in medical studies. But then, in an instant, it was all ripped away. And Rubi, who was classed as clinically dead for 10 minutes, claims her current life was “erased” as she was transported to a parallel timeline for five years.

‌



“I didn’t leap into another place or time,” the medical student said. “My life simply seemed to continue – day-by-day – from 2025 until 2030. “The future world was more advanced and peaceful than the one I had left behind. We weren’t so dependent on mobile phones. Technology had automated common tasks so that people had more time for socialising.

‌



View 4 Images Rubi says she also ended up in hospital in her future timeline

“I still had my job, but I spent most of my time with my husband and the rest of my family. As the years passed, all of us got older, as we would have done during those five years.”

Rubi, from Mexico, had started her day in April 2025 like normal. By midday, though, she was on the phone pleading to her husband, who she doesn’t wish to name, for help. She wasn’t able to move her legs and was struggling to breathe.

‌



Her oxygen levels quickly plummeted to 65% – which is lethal. At the hospital, it was found she had suffered a bilateral pulmonary thromboembolism, where blood clots obstruct arteries in both lungs.

She said: “I don’t remember anything about this day. It’s a complete blank. I was suffocating from within. Two massive blood clots had formed and blocked both my right and left pulmonary arteries. I had a total blockage.”

View 4 Images Rubi in hospital

‌



At 10pm, Rubi had her first cardiac arrest and just five hours later, her heart stopped beating. She said: “This time, I was clinically dead for more than ten minutes. When doctors restarted my heart, my pupils were dilated and fixed; showing no reaction to light or stimuli. I was declared brain dead.

“They told my parents there was nothing more they could do.”

It was planned for Rubi to be transported back home, where she would remain on life support indefinitely. In her alternate reality, though, things were also turning dark. She said: “I suffered a traumatic attack by three men at a party in this timeline. I ended up in hospital in that world, too, as if my trauma was echoing across both realities. It was painful, complicated and exhausting.”

‌



Suddenly, her body “zapped” back into the physical world as she passed through a “hellish” tunnel filled with her greatest fears.

A light flashed twice, which she touched, and brought her back to life. Rubi, however, was not relieved to be waking up. She said: “That was my real hell – waking up in this life.

View 4 Images Rubi says the future is peaceful

‌



“I had multiple surgeries during my coma, but I never felt a thing. The pain came when I woke up. I was unable to speak, told I had permanent brain damage and that I would never walk again. Everyone was shocked to see me back.

“I was confused when I saw my brother, as he looked so much younger than he did the last time I had seen him – in 2030. I was so afraid of the attackers in the other world that I pleaded for help. Soon, I realised I had been in a coma for a month and that the other world wasn’t real.

Article continues below

“It took me quite a while to understand I had time-travelled.”

Now, she’s sharing her story in search of answers and to show people that death isn’t truly the end. She added: “I’ve felt a deeper spiritual connection than I had before. Sharing my story has allowed me to bring hope to so many people who are looking for answers.

“Death is not a wall – but a doorway to a life that never truly ends.”

News.title: UK milk, bread, cheese and eggs supplier plunges into liquidation as industry in chaos
News.content:
UK milk, bread, cheese and eggs supplier plunges into liquidation as industry in chaos

A UK milk, bread, cheese and eggs supplier known for providing the 'highest quality products' has plunged into liquidation as the dairy industry is in chaos with the cost of milk increasing

View 2 Images The dairy company has gone into liquidation (Image: Getty )

A UK milk, bread, cheese and eggs supplier has plunged into liquidation as the dairy industry is in chaos.

‌



Ever Fresh Dairy, based in London, is ending business with liquidators assigned on Thursday, March 19.

‌



The company provided dairy products including milk, bread, butter, eggs and yogurt to customers. They claim to have been a "progressive and fast-growing company, well known for its high quality and Dairy products."

‌



The business stocked clients with the "highest quality achievable" with years of experience. Ever Fresh Dairy had a blend of their own milk with deliberately chosen ingredients.

Their website reads: "We adore dairy. It's at the core of all that we do."

‌



On March 19 two joint liquidators were assigned by creditors. Robert Neil Dymon and Joanne Louise Hammond of BTG Begbies Traynor in Northampton.

View 2 Images Cows in a field

The closure of Ever Fresh Dairy comes as the dairy industry is in chaos with prices paid to farmers significantly slashed.

Article continues below

According to NFUS prices for mild cheddar, butter and skimmed milk powder are all approaching their lowest levels for five years.

Large dairy processors like Arla, Muller and First Milk have made cuts to the price they pay farmers for their milk over the past months, in what they say is in response to the global markets.

Despite the spiked costs, milk production is at an all time high, expected to exceed 13 billion litres in the UK this year.

News.title: Dad loses eye after stranger caught it with nail in pool on holiday
News.content:
Dad loses eye after stranger caught it with nail in pool on holiday

They thought it was a nick, but the damage was beyond repair

View 4 Images Lee returned to the UK in a bid to get treatment

A dad has had top have his eyeball removed after it was scratched by stranger’s fingernail in a holiday accident. Lee Cuthbert had been playing volleyball with his children, Mia, and Charlie in their hotel pool.

‌



The game quickly turned into a friendly competition as other holiday-goers got involved. But the 46-year-old, from Leicester, was left with blood streaming from his right eye. His wife, Rachael, 41, was "horrified" when she opened her husband’s eyelid to see the damage.

‌



She said: “I gasped with horror as I saw his eye. He told me one of the other players had caught him with their nail when they reached out for the ball. It dug in and slashed his eye right in the middle. I couldn’t help but panic as I rushed to find help.”

‌



View 4 Images Lee in Mexico

Rachael, Lee and their two kids had jetted off to Mexico for two weeks in an all-inclusive resort. After the accident, a nurse was thankfully nearby who urged the family to rush to hospital. Rachael stayed with the children as Lee’s parents whisked him off to be seen.

When he returned the next morning, though, she learned the true reality of his “nick”. She said: “He had a huge bandage covering his eye. It was stitched back together, but it was only temporary. When the player hit him, his eyeball exploded instantly.

‌



View 4 Images Lee and Rachael in Mexico

“Lee would never get his sight back and it took a while for him to accept this. It was red raw inside as I cleaned it carefully. Our trip had been ruined as he had to stay cooped up in the bedroom away from any sunlight or water.”

A week into their trip in October 2017, the family was told to fly back to the UK. Daily tasks, such as making a cup of tea, became impossible as he wasn’t able to see what he was doing properly.

Article continues below

View 4 Images Lee's eye could not be saved

And then, a year later, he had to get part of his eye removed and replaced with a prosthetic. Luckily, the result looked “so real” that the bricklayer’s anxiety began to subside. The family filed a claim through their insurer, who paid out £15,000.

Now, they’ve come to terms with their new normal – and Lee hasn’t been put off playing in pools. Rachael added: “He still loves snorkelling or playing water games. He’s quickly returned to my daredevil hubby.”

News.title: 'David after Dentist' is now 25 and looks unrecognisable from boy who garnered 143m views
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: 'David after Dentist' is now 25 and looks unrecognisable from boy who garnered 143m views

It has been 17 years since the 'David after Dentist' video was uploaded to YouTube and since then it has been viewed 143 million times — and the Mirror has spoken to the viral kid who is now an adult

View 6 Images A video of seven-year-old David has been seen 143m times on YouTube (Image: David Devore Jr)

A viral sensation known as ‘David after Dentist’ is now 25 years old — and still gets recognised 17 years on from his hilarious post tooth removal surgery ramblings.

‌



David DeVore, from Florida in the US, was seven when he famously asked “is this real life” while his dad filmed his loopy reaction to anaesthetic treatment. The YouTube video has been seen a staggering 143 million times — and it is considered to be one of the platform’s first homemade viral hits.

‌



Almost two decades on, David spoke to The Mirror about what life looks like now, and whether he is still recognised as being the kid from the dentist video. He told us: “People have actually recognised me a bit more in recent years now that I have done interviews etc as an adult. It’s been a fun change of pace!”

‌



David spoke to this reporter three years ago while he was in his fourth year at the University of Florida. And asked for a life update, he now said: “Things have been great! Since we last spoke, I graduated with a Bachelor's Degree in computer science.

View 6 Images Do you remember this video? (Image: David Devore Jr)

“Following graduation, I started working a remote job that allowed me to follow my girlfriend to Atlanta, Georgia, and enjoy post-grad life in a fun city.

‌



“I also recently started my master’s degree, also in computer science, at Georgia Tech. It’s been a fun season of life, learning a lot and enjoying being on my own as I build my life. I have also gotten to travel a ton!” The famous video is still available to watch on YouTube but it only made it onto the streaming platform by chance.

David’s father initially filmed it solely because his wife was out of town. However, after showing it to friends and relatives and gauging their reactions, he then decided to put it on YouTube seven months after it was recorded.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



In the memorable video, David was asked how the tooth extraction went and he replied: “I didn’t feel anything… I feel funny… is this real life?” He added: “You have four eyes. I feel funny. Why is this happening to me?”

His dad said “it’s okay bud, it’s just from the medicine” — before David asked: “Is this going to be forever?” However, the clip ended up being everlasting, and it garnered three million views within three days.

David described it as the “biggest blessing” and life changed in an instant. Him and his family were even flown to LA to be on the red carpet with other viral kids for the Ralph Breaks the Internet premier.

‌



Speaking to this reporter in March 2023, he said: “There are nothing but positive experiences. We have gotten to do things, see things and go to places we never would have.

View 6 Images This is how David looks now (Image: David Devore Jr)

“And some of the most bizarre interactions with strangers were a lot closer to the time the video came out.

‌



“When we were in New York for the Today show people were spotting me across Times Square. Then when I was 13, like six years later, my family was at a restaurant and the chef in the kitchen saw me through the kitchen window and recognised me somehow. It was crazy stuff like that.”

David also felt fortunate that it became viral in 2009 when he was only seven as opposed to something like that happening in today’s world.

View 6 Images David looks much different to the kid who went viral (Image: David Devore)

‌



He said he had no comprehension of how big the video became at the time and that this allowed him to “just go with the flow” and not let it become a bigger part of him than it was.

David acknowledged that it could have influenced his thinking had he been older and he is thankful it never became his personality.

He has gone through life without telling peers about the video, but inevitably they often find out.

‌



View 6 Images David pictured with his girlfriend (Image: David Devore Jr)

And in 2021 he hit the headlines after the original unedited version of the clip was sold as an NFT for $11,600 (approx £8,700).

This money helped pay for David and his brother’s education and despite not liking to dwell on it, he did make one confession.

‌



He laughed: “I try not to take advantage of it too hard but to get into the University of Florida you have to have certain academic merit but they also put a lot of emphasis on the essay you have to write…

“So I really milked the 'David After Dentist' thing in the essay and I got in so I don’t know whether it did or didn’t have an impact but I tried.

View 6 Images The video racked up millions of views within days (Image: David Devore Jr)

Article continues below

“You had to talk about something unique in your life that had an impact on you and taught you something that has been valuable as a potential student.

“So I used that to talk about some of the unique things I was able to experience and things like that.”
